title: How to Raise Money: Paul Graham's rules for seed fundraising
summary: Graham gives founders a simple rule set for phase 2 (seed) fundraising: stay out of fundraising until you decide to raise, talk to investors in parallel ranked by expected value, treat anything short of a firm offer as a no, and accept acceptable offers quickly. Fundraising is a means to an end; the real test is revenue, so get it over with and get back to making things and talking to users.

principles.text: Be in fundraising mode or not; it is so distracting that you should focus fully, finish fast, and get back to work.
principles.quote: Because fundraising is so distracting, a startup should either be in fundraising mode or not.

principles.text: Treat every investor as a no until they give a definite offer with no contingencies, and get commitments confirmed.
principles.quote: Treat investors as saying no till they unequivocally say yes, in the form of a definite offer with no contingencies.

principles.text: Talk to investors in parallel, prioritized by expected value (chance they say yes times how good it would be).
principles.quote: When you talk to investors your m.o. should be breadth-first search, weighted by expected value.

principles.text: Judge investors by actions, and always ask what happens next and what they need to decide.
principles.quote: Never leave a meeting with an investor without asking what happens next.

principles.text: Valuation is not what matters. Priorities are getting the money you need, then good investors, with valuation at best third.
principles.quote: The number one thing you want from phase 2 fundraising is to get the money you need, so you can get back to focusing on the real test, the success of your company.

principles.text: Accept acceptable offers greedily rather than waiting for something better; investors who only invest after others do are worth nothing early.
principles.quote: If someone makes you an acceptable offer, take it.
